NutriCorp Holdings Inc. - Q3 Fiscal 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the NutriCorp Holdings Inc. Q3 Fiscal 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. Today's conference call is being recorded. At this time, I would like to inform you that this call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson (Head of Investor Relations):
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss NutriCorp Holdings Inc.'s Q3 Fiscal 2024 results. Joining me on the call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Jane Harrington, Chief Financial Officer; Mike Chen, Chief Growth Officer; and Lisa Patel, Chief Supply Chain Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from these statements.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera (CEO):
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. We are pleased to report our results for Q3 Fiscal 2024. We delivered strong performance despite ongoing macroeconomic headwinds and inflationary pressures.

Today, I'll be focusing on six key areas: updates on M&A activity and portfolio management, discussion of pricing actions and revenue growth management strategies, overall company performance highlights, EBITDA margin performance and key factors, impact of foreign exchange rates on revenue, and market share trends for major brands.

First, regarding updates on M&A activity and portfolio management. Our efforts remain central to our "Power Up the Portfolio" strategy. In this rapidly shifting Food & Beverage industry, with consumers prioritizing health, sustainability, and convenience amid post-pandemic habits and 7-9% food inflation, we've stayed disciplined in capital allocation toward high-conviction assets. We're aiming for at least 80% of net revenues from power brands growing at double-digit rates, while pruning non-core assets to fuel organic growth and margin expansion.

In Q2, we closed the $1.2 billion acquisition of VerdeSnacks, a top U.S. producer of plant-based snack bars and extruded puffs like GreenBite and VitaCrunch, perfectly aligning with our functional nutrition platform. It brought $280 million in trailing twelve-month revenues with 12% organic growth in 2022, driven by over 25% e-commerce sales, similar to trends at Kellogg's RXBAR or Mondelēz's bars. Integration is ahead of plan, with $45 million in run-rate synergies from supply chain optimization through our Global Procurement Network, using AI-driven forecasting to cut raw material costs 8-10% on nuts, seeds, and pea proteins. VerdeSnacks' EBITDA margins have risen 250 basis points to 18%, and we project 75 basis points of EPS accretion in FY2025.

In early Q3, we divested the legacy U.S. canned soup business, Homestead Hearty, to a private equity group for $450 million in cash at a 9.5x multiple on 2022 EBITDA. This generated $320 million after-tax proceeds, deployed into share repurchases and debt reduction, dropping net leverage to 2.8x from 3.2x at 2023 year-end. The soups unit had $180 million in annual sales but only 1-2% organic growth amid declining at-home cooking and competition from premium ready-meals like HelloFresh or Campbell's updates. Now, non-core assets are under 5% of our portfolio, down from 12% three years ago, freeing resources for high-growth areas where we're gaining 15-20% market share.

Internationally, APAC, which fueled 22% of Q3 revenue growth, saw us sign a binding agreement for a 51% stake in Thai-based TropiPure Beverages for $650 million. It offers low-sugar RTD functional drinks like coconut water hybrids and kombucha, with $220 million TTM sales and 18% CAGR over three years, capitalizing on Southeast Asia's wellness surge where plant-based beverages jumped 35% since 2020 per Nielsen. This bolsters our Thailand and Indonesia presence as urban millennials swap sugary colas like Coca-Cola's Fanta for premiums. We anticipate $30 million synergies by blending their 80% ASEAN tropical fruit sourcing with our precision fermentation for longer shelf life, aiming for 22% EBITDA margins post-close in H1 2025.

In EMEA, with softer sentiment and 10%+ inflation, we've paused bolt-ons but formed a $150 million JV with a Danish dairy co-op for A2 milk protein yogurts under NutriPure, leveraging their 40% Nordic premium dairy share against Unilever's plant-dairy like The Vegetarian Butcher. Pilots show 25% repeat rates, setting us for 10-12% category growth with EU sugar reduction rules.

Our portfolio playbook centers on premiumization, health & functionality, and snacking occasions. We've shed $1.8 billion in underperforming SKUs since 2021, like regional candies and low-margin private-labels, lifting our portfolio health score from 72 to 88 out of 100. Power brands like VitaFuel protein shakes up 14% YoY, EarthCrunch plant chips at 19%, and PureSip hydration at 16% in NA now drive 82% of revenues with 9% organic growth versus industry 4-5% per IRI/Circana.

We're accelerating with our Portfolio AI Engine on Snowflake and Palantir, analyzing 2.5 petabytes of POS, social, and supply data to spot $200 million FY2025 opportunities, like dynamic assortment boosting NA on-shelf availability 15%. In LATAM, up 28% YoY, we've localized 60% savory snacks with cassava alternatives, cutting imports 12% amid Brazil's 20% snacking boom.

These moves de-risk against volatility, with global F&B M&A down 25% YoY per Bain due to rates. Our $2.5 billion dry powder plus $800 million divestiture proceeds targets 2-3 accretive deals yearly through 2025 at >15% ROIC. We see M&A driving 200 bps margin expansion in FY2025, with 7-9% revenue growth, 6% organic, 1-3% inorganic. This transforms NutriCorp into a functional F&B leader resilient to inflation and diet shifts.

Second, concerning discussion of pricing actions and revenue growth management strategies. These are core to resilient top-line growth as one of our four pillars alongside volume, innovation, and portfolio shape. In Q3, they powered 4.2% organic net revenue growth, with pricing at +6.8 points offsetting -1.9% volume and +0.3% mix, amid 5-7% input inflation on cocoa, coffee, oils.

Global ASP rose 7.1% YoY, beating our 6-7% H1 guide: 60% list price carryover from Q2, 25% trade hikes, 15% optimized promotions preserving margins. Elasticity at -0.4 beat category -0.6 per IRI/Nielsen, via occasion/channel/shopper segmentation, unlike Hershey's steeper hikes eroding share.

Beverages led at +9.2%, with VitaQuench up 12% ASP shifting to $4.99 multipacks, gaining 150 bps vs Gatorade in c-stores. Snacks +6.5% with 4-6% resets amid 25% cocoa rise, elasticized BOGO to 35% off lifting trade efficiency 220 bps to 22% revenue, distribution +1.2%. Dairy/plant-based +5.8%, yogurt pods +8% with AI pilots like Danone.

NA (45% revenue) +8.1% pricing gained 90 bps ACV per Circana, co-developing hero SKUs like $3.49 pretzels undercutting private label at 45% margins despite Walmart/Kroger pressure. Europe +5.9% on health premiums like 10% organic nut butters. EM +11.4%, India/Brazil 14% on indulgent chocolates/stick packs reaching 5M households.

Our PriceForge AI/ML on IRI/Nielsen/Kantar simulates 10,000 scenarios weekly for 5,000 SKUs, hitting 95% forecast accuracy, hyper-local elasticity. Smart stacking cut low-ROI promos 30%, redirecting $150M to displays at 3:1 ROI. Resealable pouches +4% ASP like Coca-Cola's pods.

RGM embeds in Total Consumer Value: entry SKUs flat like $1.29 crackers, premium at 2x rates to 28% sales. Q4 pricing +6-7%, +100 bps organic via zero-sugar PureSpark. Risks like EM FX, Nestlé EDLP managed by elasticity database/war rooms. This expanded gross margins 180 bps to 42.3%, fueling sustainable growth.

Third, in terms of overall company performance highlights. For Q3 ended September 30, 2024, we posted net sales of $18.7 billion, up 9.2% YoY, organic 7.1% from 4.2% volume, 2.5% pricing, 0.4% mix—ninth straight quarter over 5%, beating global F&B 3-4% per NielsenIQ/Euromonitor.

Adjusted operating income $3.9 billion at 20.8% margin, +180 bps, from pricing, efficiencies, premium shift. Adjusted EPS $1.72, +14.5%, aided by $1.2B debt refi at <4%, $2.8B of $5B buybacks.

EBITDA $4.8 billion, 25.6% margin +210 bps. FCF $2.1 billion +22% YoY funded $1.1B dividends—52nd year increases—net debt/EBITDA 2.1x vs 2.5x target.

Beverages (55%, $10.3B) +8.4% organic, Gatorade Zero/Propel at 12% NA sports share per IRI, COGS/case -2% via Ginkgo precision fermentation cutting sugar 15%. Snacks (30%, $5.6B) +11.2%, Lay's Kettle +18%, Hippeas $250M run-rate to 20% plant snacks, margins +250 bps to 24.1% via ADM regen ag +10% almond yield.

Nutritionals (15%, $2.8B) +22.7%, Pure Protein/Quest +30% on GLP-1 tailwinds, MushFuel pilots for $12B adaptogens at 9% CAGR.

NA (60%) +10.5%, +1.2 pts to 28% share per Circana, e-comm 18%. EMEA (20%) +3.2% despite inflation, Walkers less salt +2 pts, Cocoa Horizon 70% certified +4% premium. APAC (12%) +16.8%, China Tingyi +20%, India Mirinda +12%. LATAM +6.1% despite FX.

Thrive25 pillars: health (45% pipeline better-for-you), supply resilience, digital. $450M R&D, Singapore CoE. SAP 85% live saved $250M procurement, Palantir 92% forecast amid sugar +15%. Scope 3 -12% via Indigo Ag.

FY24: organic 7-8%, EPS $6.95-7.05 +11-12%, EBITDA 25.5%.

Fourth, looking at EBITDA margin performance and key factors. Adjusted EBITDA margin hit 18.5%, +130 bps YoY from 17.2%, +70 bps sequential, TTM 18.2% at high end vs PepsiCo/Mondelez 16-17%.

Gross margin +190 bps to 44.1%: pricing +250 bps (4-6% on 70% SKUs, elasticity -1.2% vs -2.5%), mix +100 bps (RTD bev 22% at 52% margins, BFY snacks +15%), offset commodity +150 bps headwind (cocoa +25% hedged 70%, dairy/sugar +3/+2%). Labor +5% offset by robotics $25M save +40 bps.

SG&A -60 bps to 25.6% on 7% growth: ZBB marketing digital shift 3:1 ROMI, SAP 80% live -7% indirects.

NA (55%) +220 bps to 21.3% on bev/snack pricing. APAC (20%) +310 bps to 17.8% Indonesia/India RTD coffee +12% vol. EMEA (15%) -50 bps to 15.2% FX/reg, offset pricing/low-margin cuts. LATAM (10%) flat 14.5% BRL/wheat, local corn 65%.

Initiatives: IBM Food Trust blockchain 40% supply -12% waste premium clean-label; ML demand sensing +18% accuracy -$40M inventory; regen farming -5% fertilizer, Scope 3 -25% $10M green finance.

FY24 guide 18.0-18.5%, Q4 holiday/$1.2B FCF +10%, FY25 19-20% via $500M dairy divest, $300M capex aseptic for 15% CAGR RTD/functional.

Fifth, reviewing impact of foreign exchange rates on revenue. With 60% revenue international on $10.2B TTM, FX was key. Q3 net revenue $2.48B -2.1% reported, +4.2% CC (5.1% vol/mix, 1.2% pricing), $128M or 5.0 pts FX headwind vs $95M Q2.

70% translational $90M, 30% transactional $38M. Europe (28%) $62M -8.2%, EUR whipsaw -6.4% reported vs +1.8% CC, plant dairy +7%. APAC (22%) $28M -4.1%, JPY +5.2% hurt hydration, IDR tailwind +6.3% teas, flat reported $546M. LATAM (15%) $24M -7.6%, BRL -11%/MXN -6% -9.2% vs +3.4% CC. Other EM $14M -9.8%, TRY -15%. NA (27%) +2.3%.

USD strength DXY +7.2%, Q4 $80-100M headwind. Hedging 65% transactional 1.08 USD/EUR, natural 55% local source APAC/LATAM, pricing +150 bps. $250M capex Vietnam/Brazil localize, FX contracts, India to 10% mix.

Sixth, analyzing market share trends for major brands. Per Nielsen/IRI/Circana through October, +1.8 ppt aggregate to 14.2% NAB/9.7% snacks vs flat/-0.5%.

Beverages (62%): ZestCola #2 CSD 22.4% +1.2 ppt zero-sugar +4.1% velocity c-stores 28%. VitalBoost energy 11.8% +2.7 ppt vs Red Bull/Monster, Boost Bar nootropics TikTok e-comm +15%, ACV 92%. PureFizz sparkling 16.7% +3.1 vs Bubly, electrolytes repeat +22%.

Snacks (28%): NutriCrunch savory 13.9% +1.4 vs Lay's, air-fried low-sodium 8% BFY. PowerBite bars 7.2% +1.9 post-IndieBar.

NA (85%) +2.2 ppt Sun Belt c-stores. Europe +0.8 to 8.4 ZestCola Light rPET. APAC +3.5 to 11.2 VitalBoost China 9.8 lychee Tmall. LATAM +0.4 NutriCrunch tortilla Mexico 6.1.

Pillars: 14 SKUs like BrewVital RTD coffee 4.2% share $15B 9% CAGR; Velocity 2.0 ACV 89%, Walmart+ +11%; pricing 42.3% margins +20% ad CTV clean label. FY24 15.1% bev/10.4% snacks, $200M pipeline GLP-1 low-cal, quick comm 2-3 ppt.

Overall, we are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jane Harrington to provide more detail on our financial results.

Jane Harrington (CFO):
Thank you, Alex. As Alex mentioned, we achieved solid results in Q3 Fiscal 2024. Net sales were $18.7 billion, representing a 9.2% increase year-over-year. Gross margin was 44.1%, impacted by favorable pricing and mix shifts partially offset by commodity inflation. Operating income was $3.9 billion, and earnings per share were $1.72. We are managing our costs effectively and continue to invest in key growth initiatives.

Our balance sheet remains strong with $4.5 billion in cash and marketable securities. We are committed to returning value to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases.

For the full year, we are reaffirming our guidance for organic sales growth of 7-8%, adjusted EPS of $6.95-$7.05, and EBITDA margins of 25.5%.

Now, let's open the call for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, if you would like to ask a question at this time, please press star then one on your touchtone telephone. To withdraw your question, please press star then two. We'll pause momentarily to assemble the queue. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please proceed.

John Smith (Goldman Sachs):
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of inflation on your business?

Alex Rivera (CEO):
Good morning, John. Inflation remains a challenge at 5-7% across key inputs like cocoa up 25%, coffee, and oils, but our RGM strategies have turned it into a tailwind. Pricing delivered +6.8 points to organic growth, with ASP +7.1% and elasticity -0.4, far better than peers. We've passed through costs via targeted hikes, hedging 70% commodities, and efficiencies like AI procurement saving 8-10%, expanding gross margins 180-190 bps. This positions us resiliently as we balance affordability on entry SKUs with premium growth.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with JPMorgan. Please proceed.

Emily Chen (JPMorgan):
What are your plans for new product launches and what is the expected impact?

Mike Chen (Chief Growth Officer):
Thanks, Emily. Our innovation pipeline is robust, with 14 new SKUs this year like zero-sugar PureSpark sodas at +15% ASP and BrewVital plant-based RTD coffees targeting the $15B segment at 9% CAGR, already capturing 4.2% share. MushFuel adaptogens and GLP-1 compatible low-cal options aim for 2-3 ppt gains in quick commerce. Post-VerdeSnacks and TropiPure, these will add 1-2% inorganic growth, boosting power brands to 82% revenues and driving 7-9% total top-line with margin accretion.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Lee with Morgan Stanley. Please proceed.

David Lee (Morgan Stanley):
How are you managing supply chain disruptions?

Lisa Patel (Chief Supply Chain Officer):
Good question, David. We've built resilience via localization—55% APAC/LATAM production local, up from 42%, and $250M capex for Vietnam/Brazil plants. Global Procurement Network with AI forecasting cuts costs 8-10%, SAP/Palantir improves forecasts 92-95%, reducing stockouts 30%. Regen ag with ADM/Indigo -12% Scope 3, blockchain 40% traceability -12% waste. For disruptions like Black Sea wheat or West Africa cocoa, hedging and diversified sourcing like Midwest dairy co-ops keep COGS stable, supporting FCF $2.1B.

Operator:
Our last question comes from Sarah Kim with Barclays. Please proceed.

Sarah Kim (Barclays):
What is your outlook for the rest of the year?

Jane Harrington (CFO):
Thanks, Sarah. We're reaffirming FY24 guidance: 7-8% organic sales, EPS $6.95-7.05 midpoint +12%, EBITDA 25.5%. Q4 sees holiday acceleration, pricing +6-7%, RGM +100 bps, moderating FX $80-100M headwind. M&A like TropiPure adds inorganic, share gains 1.8 ppt aggregate, FCF up 10% funds buybacks/dividends. Risks like cocoa volatility managed by hedges, positioning for FY25 19-20% EBITDA margins and 10%+ EPS growth.

Operator:
I would now like to turn the call back over to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera (CEO):
Thank you for your questions and your continued interest in NutriCorp Holdings Inc. We are focused on executing our strategy and delivering strong results. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
